messages:
alex: :rotating_light: customer report — multiple customers seeing 502/504s hitting hosted API around 11:22-11:38 UTC. They pasted curl output showing intermittent 502 from /v1/generate. can we triage?

maria: seeing the same in logs. spike started at 2025-09-03T11:22:10Z. envoys returning 502 -> upstream reset. sample envoy log:
```
[2025-09-03T11:22:12.345Z] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2" 502 NR - 0 0 12 12 "-" "curl/7.68.0" "-" "10.2.3.45:443" "upstream_reset"
```

jordan: attaching a couple of request headers we saw — some requests have a new long header `X-Billing-Meta` added by billing service (~3.8kB). not present before the billing rollout this morning.

kai: that could matter. large headers + high concurrency can push h2 buffers and upstream connection pool behavior. but I'd expect 431 or 400 if headers exceed size, not 502. what's upstream (nginx/gunicorn) showing?

maria: upstream NGINX shows connection resets, a lot of `recv()` errors and `upstream prematurely closed connection`. excerpt: 
```
2025/09/03 11:22:13 [error] 12345#0: *98765 recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.7, server: hosted-api, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2.0", upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/", host: "api.redwood.example"
```

alex: timeline hypothesis: billing rollout injected large header on a subset of requests. combined with a backend model cold start (~1500ms) and increased concurrency we exhausted the upstream worker keepalive/connections -> upstream closed connections -> envoy returned 502. monitoring shows a concurrent request bump at same time.

ops-bot: ALERT: hosted-api.edge.502_rate increase — 11:22:10 to 11:38:05 — peak 4.5% 502s across edge cluster. traces with distributed sampling: 62% of 502s share header pattern `X-Billing-Meta: len>3000`.

jordan: repro steps I used:
```
# simulate long billing header + concurrent requests
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Billing-Meta: $(head -c 3500 /dev/urandom | base64)" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
I get ~15% 502s locally against staging edge with the new billing-header attached.

kai: nice repro. mitigation options: roll back the billing header injection, increase envoy buffer limits, or add a quick gateway rule that strips `X-Billing-Meta` to the edge (only for hosted-api route) until billing fixes the payload size. happy path: strip header at edge -> allow traffic to normal backends.

maria: ops playbook commands to find traces/logs:
```
jq -r '.entries[] | select(.status==502) | .request.id' /var/log/edge/requests.jsonl | xargs -n1 -I{} curl -s https://traces/api/{}
# grep for header pattern
rg "X-Billing-Meta" /var/log/edge/requests.jsonl | head
```

support-bot: draft for customers: "We're investigating intermittent 502/504s affecting some tokenized requests. We have identified a correlation with a newly added billing header and are applying a temporary mitigation. We will update within 60 minutes." :thumbsup:

alex: action items:
- kai: implement header-strip rule on edge for hosted-api route (canary to 10% traffic) — timeboxed 30m
- jordan: coordinate rollback of billing header rollout / set size cap in billing service
- maria: monitor 502 rate, share dashboard link and sample trace ids
- support-bot: send customer update (initial)

kai: starting header-strip canary now. rule: remove `X-Billing-Meta` for requests to `/v1/*` coming from billing cluster id `billing-prod`. config snippet I'm using: 
```
route:
  match: "/v1/*"
  actions:
    - remove_header: "X-Billing-Meta"
    - weight: 10%
```
pushing in 2m.

maria: dashboard link: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/hosted-api/errors?window=30m — 502 spike visible. sample trace ids: tr-0a1b2c3d, tr-0f9e8d7c

ops-bot: NOTE: canary applied by kai at 11:29:40Z. 5m check expected.

alex: good. if canary reduces 502s to baseline we can extend and then fully remove header at edge. keep me posted.

jordan: billing team confirmed they pushed a hotfix to truncate `X-Billing-Meta` to 512 bytes at 11:35Z. they also started a rollback plan if needed.

maria: follow-up metrics after canary (11:35-11:45): 502s dropped from 4.5% -> 0.6% cluster-wide. traces no longer show `len>3000` headers.

support-bot: customer update sent at 11:47Z: "Mitigation applied; we observed recovery. Root cause under investigation (billing header size + upstream connection exhaustion). Next update in 2 hours or sooner."

alex: postmortem tasks assigned:
- eng-runtime: add header-size based early-reject or 431 path with clearer error (owner: jordan)
- eng-traffic: add docs and a lint rule for header size in onboarding for services (owner: kai)
- billing: permanently cap injected header length and add tests (owner: billing-team)

kai: thanks team. I'll follow up with config diff and the canary runbook. :white_check_mark:
